topic: Radius of Gyration and Moments of Inertia of Common Bodies
title: Ring or Disc? Radius of Gyration Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A bicycle wheel keeps its weight at the rim. A machine flywheel is heavy at its edge. A grinding stone is solid all through. And when Aarav gives a ring and a disc of the same mass the same push, the disc whirls faster. Why? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we meet the radius of gyration and the moments of inertia of common bodies.

On a live motion notebook a disc spins beside a ring of the same mass that slowly shrinks, while the readout tracks the ring's radius and both moments of inertia, and a graph shows the ring's I sliding down its curve until it meets the disc's line at k. A slow-mo replay freezes the match. We derive k = R/root 2 for a disc step by step, see link by link why a disc's k sits inside its rim, learn the NCERT table (ring, disc, rod, solid sphere), compare ring and disc side by side, and find I and k for a rod. Then the exam trap (k = R/2 is only for a diameter), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
